data.content_ref: inline:The protocol claims that if evidence had been completed, anti-entropy would ensure at least one node observed the non-null hash and refused to sign a null attestation. However, the problem states the process crashes while holding the workspace and leaves no terminal record. If the process finished computing the deterministic evidence locally but crashed before any gossip or anti-entropy exchange, every surviving node genuinely lacks knowledge of the evidence and may correctly sign a null attestation. Once f+1 null witnesses are gathered, reclamation proceeds and the completed evidence in the crashed workspace is silently displaced. The causal witnessing assumption therefore collapses under the exact crash-before-communication scenario the problem describes, so the gossip quorum fails the required guarantee.
